```{r,include=FALSE}
library(vegan)

library(ape)       # For plotting trees

```

Now load the the data from the previous lab (change path to the file if
necessary):


# Distance metrics

Let's calculate the Bray Curtis dissimilarities for the rarefied dataset
Bray–Curtis dissimilarity ranges from 0 to 1:
* 0: Identical OTU abundance profiles.
* 1: No shared OTUs.
* Between 0 and 1: Increasing differences in OTU composition and relative abundance.


```{r}
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray <- vegdist(otu.vegan.ss.nozero, method = "bray") # calculated distance
as.matrix(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray)[1:5, 1:5]
```

- *What kind of data is the Bray-Curtis dissimilarity suitable for?*
- *How can you change the dissimilarity index in the previous chunk of
  code?*

# Ordination and clustering

## PCA

Pca from the rarefied table

```{r}
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.pca <- PCAtools::pca(t(otu.vegan.ss.nozero), scale = FALSE) # Runs the PCA
PCAtools::biplot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.pca, showLoadings = TRUE, x = "PC1", y = "PC2", lab = rownames(otu.vegan.ss.nozero)) # Plots the PCA
screeplot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.pca, axisLabSize = 7, titleLabSize = 22) # We plot the percentage of variance explained by each axis
```

## NMDS

We will define the function NMDS.scree() that automatically performs a
NMDS for 1-8 dimensions and plots the number of dimensions vs. stress

```{r}
set.seed(666) # Set a seed to make results reproducible
NMDS.scree <- function(x, reps = 7, ks = 1:8) {# x is the name of the distance matrix
  stresses <- sapply(ks, function(k) replicate(reps, vegan::metaMDS(x, autotransform = FALSE, k = k, trace = FALSE)$stress))
  plot(NA, xlim = range(ks), ylim = range(stresses), xlab = "# of Dimensions", ylab = "Stress",
       main = "NMDS stress plot")
  for (j in seq_along(ks)) points(rep(ks[j], reps), stresses[, j])
}
```

Using the function to determine the optimal number of dimensions Using
the rarefied table

```{r}
NMDS.scree(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray)
```

We calculate NMDS for k(dimensions)=3 for the rarefied table

```{r}
set.seed(666)  # For reproducible results
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds <- metaMDS(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray, k = 3, trymax = 50, trace = FALSE)

# Check the result
stress_value <- round(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds$stress, 3)
stress_value
```

- *Stress: How good is our NMDS?*
  < 0.05, Excellent
  0.05–0.10, Very good
  0.10–0.20, Generally usable
  0.20–0.30, Potentially misleading
  ≥ 0.30 Poor representation

# Make stressplot

```{r}
stressplot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds)
```

Simple plotting of NMDS using the base plotting functions

```{# r}
plot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds, display = "sites", type = "n")
points(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds, display = "sites", col = "red", pch = 19)

# With many samples, text labels will be crowded, so let's make them smaller
text(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds, display = "sites", cex = 0.6)
```

### Let's make nicer plots

We use the metadata for the samples that was loaded in lab I

```{r}
# inspect the the data
metadata
```

Make the date a real date and the season and year factors:

```{r}
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    date = dmy(date),
    year = as.factor(year),
    seasons = factor(seasons, levels = c("winter", "spring", "summer", "autumn"))
  )
```

Next, we generate a table of nmds scores and join it with the metadata

```{r}
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds.scores <- scores(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Sample_Name") %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "Sample_Name") %>%
  as_tibble()
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds.scores
```

Create the plot, colored by season

```{r}
# Option 1: Plot without labels (cleaner with many samples)
p1 <- ggplot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds.scores) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, colour = seasons, shape = year), size = 2) +
  coord_fixed() + ## need aspect ratio of 1!
  labs(title = "NMDS - Colored by Season") +
  theme_bw()
print(p1)
```

If you really want full sample labels (will be crowded!)

```{r}
p2 <- ggplot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.nmds.scores) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, colour = seasons), size = 1.5) +
  coord_fixed() +
  geom_text_repel(
    box.padding = 0.2,
    aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, label = Sample_Name),
    size = 1.8,
    max.overlaps = 30,  # Allow more overlaps
    force = 0.5  # Reduce repelling force
  ) +
  labs(title = "NMDS - All sample labels (crowded)") +
  theme_bw()
print(p2)
```

- *Try to colour the plot by another variable in the metadata, e.g.
  `month` or `temp_25`.*

# Clustering of samples

Allows determining the similarity between samples as well as the
organization of samples in groups. Hierarchical clustering: samples will
be organized in ranks according to their similarity and all samples will
be included in a large group Unweighted Pair-Group Method Using
Arithmetic Averages (UPGMA): This linkage method will link samples by
considering their distance to a subgroup arithmetic average. This is a
method widely used in ecology

### UPGMA

Rarefied dataset We generate 100 trees by re-sampling and then, we plot
the consensus tree

```{r}
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.upgma <- recluster.cons(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray, tr = 100, p = 0.5, method = "average")
plot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.upgma$cons) # plot consensus tree
```

We'll calculate bootstrap support values (0: bad - 100: perfect) This
allows us to know how well supported is the branching pattern **Note:
With 82 samples, bootstrapping will take a long time (several minutes
depending on your computer)**

```{r}
# set the number of boostraps:
boots <- 100
otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.upgma.boot <- recluster.boot(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.upgma$cons,
                                                      otu.vegan.ss.nozero, tr = 50, p = 0.5,
                                                      method = "average", boot = boots, level = 1)
```

## Better Tree Visualizations

```{r}
# Prepare the data
tree <- otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.upgma$cons
boot <- as.data.frame(otu.vegan.ss.nozero.bray.upgma.boot)$V1

# Colour the samples by season
season_colors <- c(winter = "steelblue", spring = "forestgreen", summer = "orange", autumn = "brown")
tip_seasons <- tibble(Sample_Name = tree$tip.label) %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "Sample_Name") %>%
  pull(seasons)
tip_colors <- season_colors[as.character(tip_seasons)]
```

### Plots with ape

```{r}
# PLOT 1: Enhanced Rectangular Tree
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
plot.phylo(tree, type = "phylogram",
           show.tip.label = TRUE,
           tip.color = tip_colors,
           cex = 0.4,  # Smaller text for many samples
           edge.width = 1.2,
           main = "UPGMA Tree - Enhanced Rectangular Layout",
           font = 2)

# Add bootstrap values with better formatting
# Only show bootstrap values ≥ 50 to reduce clutter
high_boot <- boot
high_boot[boot < 50] <- NA  # Hide low bootstrap values
nodelabels(high_boot,
           frame = "circle",
           cex = 0.5,
           col = "white",
           bg = ifelse(boot >= 70, "darkgreen",
                      ifelse(boot >= 50, "orange", "lightgray")),
           font = 2)

# Add legend for bootstrap support and seasons
legend("topleft",
       legend = c("≥70% (Strong)", "50-69% (Moderate)", "<50% (Weak)"),
       fill = c("darkgreen", "orange", "lightgray"),
       title = "Bootstrap Support",
       cex = 0.7)
legend("bottomleft",
       legend = names(season_colors),
       fill = season_colors,
       title = "Season",
       cex = 0.7)
```

### Summary Statistics and Tree Quality Assessment

```{r}
# Display tree statistics
length(tree$tip.label) # Number of tips (samples)
tree$Nnode             # Number of internal nodes
is.rooted(tree)        # Tree is rooted
is.binary(tree)        # Tree is binary

# Bootstrap support summary
summary(boot)
sum(boot >= 70, na.rm = TRUE)              # Strong support (≥70%)
sum(boot >= 50 & boot < 70, na.rm = TRUE)  # Moderate support (50-69%)
sum(boot < 50, na.rm = TRUE)               # Weak support (<50%)
```

```{r}
ggplot(tibble(boot = boot), aes(x = boot)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "lightblue", colour = "darkblue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(50, 70), colour = c("orange", "red"), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Bootstrap Support (%)", y = "Number of Nodes", title = "Distribution of Bootstrap Support Values") +
  theme_minimal()
```
